newsitem.title: USA: Western Atlas to split in two.
newsitem.headline: Western Atlas to split in two.

text.p: Western Atlas Inc., which provides oil field services and makes industrial automation equipment, will split itself in two, the company announced Monday.
Following the announcement, Western Atlas stock rose $3.875 to $65.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The oil field services business, which had $1.4 billion in revenues last year, will continue to operate as Western Atlas Inc. and will be based in Houston, the company said.

The new industrial automation company, which had $1.18 billion in 1996 revenues, will consist of Western Atlas' automated data collection, mobile computing and manufacturing systems activities. The company, which has yet to be named, will be based in Western Atlas' current headquarters city of Beverly Hills, Calif.

"The decision to separate Western Atlas' oil field services and industrial automation activities into two separate companies was made to allow each business to better focus on its distinctly different markets," said company Chairman Alton Brann.
All shares of the new industrial automation company will be distributed to holders of Western Atlas common stock, the company said.
The spinoff, which is expected to be tax-free to Western Atlas and its shareholders, should be completed by the end of 1997, the company said.
Western Atlas' current chief operating officer, John Russell, will become president and chief executive officer of the oilfield services company.
Brann will remain chairman of the board of Western Atlas, the new oil field services company, and also will become chairman and chief executive officer of the new industrial automation company.

Western Atlas' oil field services include seismic surveys, data analysis and software development. Its industrial automation units make manufacturing systems, data collection systems and other equipment for the automotive, food and beverage, aerospace and other industries.
The spinoff comes after a series of acquisitions of data collection systems companies.

Last month, Western Atlas acquired United Barcode Industries, an automated data collection company based in Sweden, making it the world's largest supplier of bar code and automated data collection network products.
In February, it acquired Norand Corp., a designer and developer of mobile computing systems and wireless data communication networks.
